QuestionStmt.S: Which of the following pair of compounds on heating gives butanenitrile?

Solution.S:
Butanenitrile is $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CN}$ (C₄H₇N). It can be prepared by nucleophilic substitution reaction of n-propyl chloride ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2Cl}$) with alcoholic KCN. The reaction is:

$$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2Cl + KCN \xrightarrow{\Delta} CH_3CH_2CH_2CN + KCl}$$

n-Propyl chloride gives butanenitrile (4 carbons). n-Butyl chloride would give pentanenitrile (5 carbons). Hence the correct option is D: n-Propylchloride and alcoholic KCN.
